## Goal and gate

Prove the owner-selected properties over explicit input boxes, calibrate uncertainty intervals,
compare coupled trajectories against Tier A physics and bind the guards to the certificates.
The brief requires CI to re-prove properties on surrogate changes. The owner certification
review is the human gate. Certification has not been granted; the owner requested further transport-bound work.

## Current review package

The four verification records, guard integration and CI re-proof are assembled for owner review. Available output certificates apply only inside exact proof boxes ([all four verified input boxes match the previous loaders; 48 of 48 retained pedestal states keep identical predictions and decisions; none of the 57 EC states is inside the exact proof boxes, so no EC certificate-based output check applies there]{.claim}[C-284](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-284){.cid .st-measured}). The owner adopted the revised report-only fallback alert policy under [OQ-50](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-50); it changes no inference decisions or physical guard tolerances. The bounded transport investigation remains scientifically unresolved after complete-box partitioning and reserved final-objective optimization ([both member-zero pilots retain overflowing physical enclosures despite complete input-box coverage; no sampled overflow witness was found, and all forty transport V5 results remain unresolved]{.claim}[C-293](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-293){.cid .st-preliminary}, [both full-box pilots retain nonfinite physical enclosures after all final objectives run; independent graph, constraint and corrected-dual replay passes, with no finite physical candidate]{.claim}[C-297](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-297){.cid .st-preliminary}). No ensemble sweep follows. Transport local robustness, EC complete local boxes and the MAST-U reference remain limitations. Historical ITER and fixed-equilibrium EC comparisons retain their original scope. Passing software checks ([1095 tests pass with two intentional heavy-proof skips in each full normal and Tier-A-only suite; lint, typing and quick verification also pass]{.claim}[C-294](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-294){.cid .st-measured}) do not grant certification.

**Historical position (26 Oct 2026).** The MAST-U remediation stopped at its reference step: no
admissible TGLF reference trajectory exists for comparing the retrained candidate, and the
projected reference of [OQ-38](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-38) cannot complete on this scenario ([150 negative raw heat diffusivities at 19 faces; 46 would reach the 1 gB stop, at 31 of 40 states, the first at state 1]{.claim}[C-240](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-240){.cid .st-measured}). The
owner limited the MAST-U scope ([OQ-42](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-42),
[entry 70](../log/70-owner-limits-the-mastu-certification-scope.qmd)): MAST-U will be presented for certification
with that limitation stated, and ITER's pass stands. The remaining work is transport output bounds, local robustness, the EC closed-loop comparison, certificate-bound
guards with a fallback-rate check, the per-surrogate reports, CI re-proofs, and then the
certification review. The paragraphs below record the remediation in order.

first run; the splitting budgets differ. See the
[technical account](../technical/verification.qmd#optimized-output-bounds).

([member 0 of each ensemble remains unknown; both processes complete in about 23 seconds, with physical inverse-transform overflow and looser intervals than the earlier optimized run]{.claim}[C-268](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-268){.cid .st-measured}); its focused checks pass ([40 focused checks pass in both normal and Tier A modes; lint, formatting and typing pass]{.claim}[C-269](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-269){.cid .st-measured}). The separated-basis diagnostic is complete and audited ([2139 integrity checks pass on the complete 54-pair basis grid and all 36 consumed-control comparisons reproduce the preceding study; electron flux changes sign at every state, steps reach 4.28 gB along the final basis and 4.11 gB along the search basis, and at the largest final basis the flux is a residual of order 1e-3 gB]{.claim}[C-205](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-205){.cid .st-measured}).
Both the width-search and final-solve basis change the flux, and they interact.
At the largest final basis the flux is a residual of order 1e-3 gB; the width
search often stops at its upper bound. Convergence is still not established.


The basis and width-range extension is complete and audited ([3029 integrity checks pass on the complete 78-pair extension and all 36 control comparisons reproduce job 2687308; NBASIS_MAX 16 still moves electron flux by up to 0.48 gB per step, and widening the width search from 1.65 to 3.3 changes it from about 1e-3 gB to as much as 181 gB]{.claim}[C-206](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-206){.cid .st-measured}).
A larger final basis does not settle the flux, and widening the width search
changes it by orders of magnitude; the standard settings act as a convention
([K-032](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-032)). [OQ-38](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-38) selects the standard-settings projected-reference convention.
That attempt is consumed and stopped at its approved limit ([the projected-reference job failed after 108 s when the log reported 3.93119 gB against the 1 gB stop limit; no completed reference was saved]{.claim}[C-217](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/claims.qmd#c-217){.cid .st-measured}).
The review fixes lost stop diagnostics and tightens future acceptance checks.
There is no completed reference, so R6/R7 and [K-030](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/ceilings.qmd#k-030) remain open. [OQ-42](/Blog/tokamak-toolkit/decisions.qmd#oq-42) then limited
